request.spec:
A claim can be shared with other people on the sheet: a person select, a share percent (two
decimals, more than 0.00) and a button on the claim (CLAIM_SHARED naming the claim, ending
with=<person> share=<share>; the claim's own person, a person already holding a share, or shares
totalling more than 100.00 are refused; a SETTLED, VOID or DELETED claim cannot be shared). Each
holder's due-total includes their part: the claim's due times their share divided by 100, rounded
half to even; the claim's own person's due-total counts the claim's due less the holders' parts,
and each person's settled-total and open-total count the same part. Show the holders on the claim as
<name> <share>, comma and space separated.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
A claim can be shared with other people on the sheet: a person select, a share percent (two
decimals, more than 0.00) and a button on the claim (CLAIM_SHARED naming the claim, ending
with=<person> share=<share>; the claim's own person, a person already holding a share, or shares
totalling more than 100.00 are refused; a SETTLED, VOID or DELETED claim cannot be shared). Each
holder's due-total includes their part: the claim's due times their share divided by 100, rounded
half to even; the claim's own person's due-total counts the claim's due less the holders' parts,
and each person's settled-total and open-total count the same part. Show the holders on the claim as
<name> <share>, comma and space separated.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
Shared claims work, and `bin/e2e` passes: all 4 tests in the spec, with every expected audit line.

**What a person sees:** each claim row now has a person select, a share-percent field and a Share button. The claim also shows its holders as `Ben 33.33, Cam 33.33`. A refused share shows the claim's error message, which clears when that row's share fields change or the next action on the row is taken.

**What the server refuses:** sharing with the claim's own person, with someone who already holds a share, with a share of 0.00 or less, or so that shares total more than 100.00. It also refuses SETTLED, VOID and DELETED claims, and people not on the sheet. A refused share writes nothing to the store and nothing to the audit file. A share that goes through writes `CLAIM_SHARED … with=<name> share=<share>`, then the usual figure records. When someone shares on behalf of a steward who delegated to them, `for=<steward>` is added on the end automatically.

**How figures change:** a holder's part is the claim's due × share ÷ 100, rounded half to even. The holder's due-total, settled-total and open-total include their part, and the claim's own person keeps the rest.

Things you might not expect:
- **A holder whose grade has no rate** still gets a due-total from their part rather than `n/a`, because the part is worked out at the claim owner's rate. The test needs this: Cam is on grade C, which has no rate.
- **Overdue totals don't move.** The request didn't mention them, so the claim's owner keeps the full overdue figure.
- **The score uses the split too**: it counts the same settled part as the settled-total.
- **The figures are worked out in two places** — on the server for the audit records, and in the browser for the screen — so I changed both. In the browser that includes the summary's per-grade due-totals and the people CSV export, which use a person's due-total.

**Storage:** a new `shares` column on the claim and its history table (migration `V93__claim_shares.sql`), so viewing the sheet as of a past date shows the shares as they stood then. The new endpoint is `POST /api/sheets/{sheetId}/claims/{claimId}/share`; the rollup change is in `RollupService.snapshot` and the browser side in `rates.ts`.

Running the front-end type check on its own reports one error, in `features/people/snapshots.slot.tsx`, a file I didn't change. The normal build doesn't run that check.
